title: Cultural Evolution Drives the Emergence of Conventions in Neural Emergent Communication
abstract: arXiv:2611.00006v2 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent studies of language evolution with neural agents often use models where agents can either speak or listen, where there are only two agents in the population, or where agents can share internal representations. These choices prevent the study of how language emerges through cultural evolution, i.e. through the cumulative adaptation of individual behaviours to fit the communicative needs of the community. We tackle this issue with a new model that trains populations of bi-directional neural agents in a fully distributed fashion to solve a referential game. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach on multiple image datasets and show that it is able to scale to large populations. We also show that more conventional languages are easier to learn, providing a direct advantage for cultural transmission. translated_title: 文化演化驱动神经涌现通信中约定惯例的产生
translated_abstract: 近期利用神经智能体进行语言演化的研究通常采用的模型中，智能体只能说话或只能倾听、种群中仅包含两个智能体、或智能体之间可以共享内部表征。这些设计选择使得无法研究语言如何通过文化演化而产生，即通过个体行为为适应群体交流需求而进行的累积性适应过程。我们通过一个新模型来解决这一问题，该模型以完全分布式的方式训练由双向神经智能体组成的种群来解决指代游戏。我们在多个图像数据集上验证了该方法的有效性，并证明其能够扩展到大规模种群。我们还表明，更加约定化的语言更容易学习，这为文化传递提供了直接优势。总体而言，这项工作为神经涌现通信提供了一种新颖的方法，为演化语言学开辟了新的研究方向。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种以完全分布式方式训练双向神经智能体种群的新模型，证明了文化演化能够驱动语言约定惯例的产生，且更约定化的语言因更易学习而在文化传递中具有直接优势。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a new model that trains populations of bi-directional neural agents in a fully distributed fashion, demonstrating that cultural evolution drives the emergence of language conventions, and that more conventional languages provide a direct advantage for cultural transmission as they are easier to learn.
